system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A process named pfupdater.exe ran from leo.martins's AppData\Roaming\PixelForge directory, rather than the inventory-listed approved location under Program Files.

That process made repeated proxy-mediated HTTPS CONNECT attempts to updates.pixelforge-suite.co, on an approximately five-minute cadence from 13:41 through 14:11 UTC. The observed hostname differs from the inventory-listed updates.pixelforge-suite.com.

Proxy records attribute these requests to a Firefox user agent, while endpoint network events associate the connections with pfupdater.exe; the proxy returned both 504 and 403 responses as well as 200 tunnel statuses.

The unexpected executable location, hostname mismatch, and user-agent/process mismatch together support treating the repeated activity as suspicious and malicious rather than as the approved updater behavior.

Other software indicators in the window include a GoogleDriveFS user agent and Dropbox updater executions; the inventory does not list those services as approved, although these records alone do not establish file sharing or data transfer by them.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, byte counts, and tunnel durations, but do not provide the HTTPS contents; a 200 status indicates a proxy tunnel, not that the destination's content was benign. (T055-00127, T055-00149, T055-00230)
The supplied records do not provide a hash, signature verification, or provenance for the AppData\Roaming\PixelForge executable. (T055-00112, T055-00113)
The GoogleDriveFS record is a proxy user-agent observation and is not tied here to a specific endpoint process or demonstrated file transfer. (T055-00050, T055-00051)
The Dropbox records show updater process execution, but no corresponding Dropbox network connection or data transfer in the supplied window. (T055-00153, T055-00156, T055-00161, T055-00166)
claims_not_established: The executable's hash, signer, source, integrity, or whether it is a legitimate per-user PixelForge updater.
Whether the .co destination is controlled by an attacker or whether any attempted HTTPS session delivered malicious content.
Whether any data was exfiltrated or what data, if any, was exchanged inside the HTTPS tunnels.
Whether GoogleDriveFS or Dropbox performed file-sharing or cloud-storage activity during this window.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire the pfupdater.exe from the reported AppData\Roaming path; calculate its hash and verify its signer, provenance, and relationship to the approved PixelForge installation.
Review proxy, DNS, TLS, and endpoint telemetry for the destination hostname, including certificate details and any available decrypted or endpoint-level request/response evidence.
Inspect the workstation for the PixelForge installation and updater configuration, persistence mechanisms, and any associated downloaded or modified files.
Determine whether GoogleDriveFS and Dropbox are installed or were used to transfer files, and review relevant file-access and network records.
